$comment: The context eval set (plan M12.6): tasks written against Friday's own repository, shaped like the tasks of a plan (a write scope and a declared read scope). Each names the files a competent engineer must read to do it (required, all inside the read scope) and globs of files that must never reach its packet (forbidden, outside the read scope). The runner tests/evals/context-evals.test.ts compiles every task's packet with the real compiler, with the declared read scope and with an open one, and scores it. Paths are repository-relative with forward slashes.

tasks.summary: friday_check_inbox tells the agent how long the messages it returns stay reserved for this session
tasks.description: The inbox tool's text ends with the reservation time Friday applied (communication.delivery_reservation_ms), so an agent knows when an unacknowledged message comes back as a new delivery.
acceptance_criteria: the MCP rig test shows the reservation time in the tool's text

tasks.summary: friday messages show counts the deliveries that ended dead
tasks.description: The per-delivery table of `friday messages show` gets a summary line with how many deliveries ended dead (delivered too often without an acknowledgement) and how many expired.
acceptance_criteria: friday messages show prints the summary line

tasks.summary: The number of uncommitted paths a packet lists comes from context.max_dirty_paths in config.yaml
tasks.description: Packets list at most 30 uncommitted paths today. The limit becomes a configuration key with that default, read by the daemon's context service and applied by the compiler, with a note when more were left out.
acceptance_criteria: a project with the key set lists that many paths

tasks.summary: A read refused by deny.read names the policy file the rule came from
tasks.description: When a hook refuses a read because a project policy file keeps the path from agents, the refusal names that file, so the agent and the human see where the rule lives.
acceptance_criteria: the hook's refusal text names the policy file

tasks.summary: GET /me tells a session the path of the worktree its task runs in
tasks.description: The harness-scoped /me answer gains the execution root of the session's current run, so an attached session can check it works in the right checkout.
acceptance_criteria: the MCP server's whoami shows the worktree path
the integration suite's daemon tests pass

tasks.summary: friday usage prints the share of whole-file reads per attempt
tasks.description: The usage table's READS W/R column is followed by the whole-file share as a percentage, null-safe: an attempt whose host reads Friday does not see shows a dash.

tasks.summary: The fake planner provider can script an invalid first answer followed by a valid repair
tasks.description: A fixture may hold two answers for one request; the fake provider returns them in order, so the Master Brain's single repair attempt is exercised without a model.
acceptance_criteria: a brain test shows the repair path with the fake provider

tasks.summary: Imports of stylesheets are recorded as unsupported edges with the reason that they are not code
tasks.description: An import whose specifier ends in .css or .scss is reported as an unsupported edge with a reason, instead of being resolved or dropped.
acceptance_criteria: a fixture with a stylesheet import lists the unsupported edge

tasks.summary: The source identity reports how many files it hashed and how many it could not
tasks.description: SourceIdentity gains counts of the changed files whose content was hashed and of those identified only by size and time, so a packet's note about an approximate identity can say how many.

tasks.summary: The agents list in the Studio can be narrowed to one role
tasks.description: The agents panel gets a role selector built from the roles present; choosing one hides the other agents, and the choice is kept for the session.
acceptance_criteria: the panel's unit tests cover the filter

tasks.summary: The Stop hook's hold names how many urgent messages wait
tasks.description: When Claude Code's Stop hook holds a session for unread urgent, high or blocking messages, its reason gives the count and points at friday_check_inbox.

tasks.summary: When a request expires unanswered, its sender gets a low-priority note from Friday
tasks.description: The lease manager's expiry of a request also queues a system note to the sender, 'Expired: <subject>', in the same transaction as the expiry event.
acceptance_criteria: the state package's messaging tests show the note

tasks.summary: providers.local.base_url must be a loopback address
tasks.description: The configuration schema refuses a local provider whose base_url is not 127.0.0.1 or ::1, with the reason, so nothing a local provider is told can leave the machine.
acceptance_criteria: a non-loopback address fails to parse with the reason

tasks.summary: A changed file outside the write scope is reported with the nearest scope glob
tasks.description: Friday's diff check against the task scope names, for each file outside it, the scope glob that comes closest, so the human sees whether the scope or the change is wrong.
acceptance_criteria: the verification tests show the glob in the finding

tasks.summary: Operations run without FRIDAY_* variables in their environment
tasks.description: The execution runner removes every FRIDAY_* variable from an operation's environment before it starts, so an operation cannot find Friday's state directory or tokens from its surroundings.
acceptance_criteria: an operation that prints its environment shows no FRIDAY_ variable

tasks.summary: The desktop tray icon's tooltip shows how many approvals wait
tasks.description: The tray's tooltip is rebuilt from the daemon's events: 'Friday: N waiting' while approvals or questions wait for a human, 'Friday' otherwise.
acceptance_criteria: the hands-on check in apps/desktop/README.md shows the tooltip
